titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Adrami, King of Rome (ch. 72)
about: The chapter tells how Rome fell to Japheth's line, how a Roman astronomer foresaw the kingship passing to the seed of David, and how King Baltasar of Rome asked Solomon for a son. Solomon, after taking counsel with Israel's elders, sends his younger son Adrami (Ardamis), who is anointed, accompanied by fourteen nobles of Israel, and married to the king's eldest daughter. The part ends with Adrami hearing his first case, a dispute over sheep and a vineyard, which breaks off before the verdict.

sentences.t: ፸፪ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ሮምሂ ።
sentences.l: 72. Concerning king-of Rome-also
sentences.i: Chapter 72: Concerning the King of Rome
sentences.n: Chapter heading. በእንተ ‘concerning’ + ንጉሠ, the construct of ንጉሥ ‘king’, + ሮም ‘Rome’: ‘king-of Rome’. The enclitic -ሂ is a mild ‘also, indeed’. The number ፸፪ is 72, spoken ሰብዓ ወክልኤ (säbʿa wä-kəlʾe). The previous part closed the chapter on the Virgin and the Incarnation; this chapter turns to the line of kings of Rome and how it came to Solomon's son.

sentences.t: ወበእንተ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ሮምሂ ፡ ንዌጥን ፡ ንንግርክሙ ፡ ዘሰማዕነ ፡ ወዘረከብነ ፡ ጽሑፈ ፡ ዘርኢነ ።
sentences.l: And-concerning king-of Rome-also we-begin we-may-tell-you what we-heard and-what we-found written, what we-saw.
sentences.i: And concerning the king of Rome also, we begin to tell you what we have heard, and what we have found written, and what we have seen.
sentences.n: ወበእንተ ‘and concerning’ (ወ- + በእንተ), then the construct ንጉሠ ሮም ‘king-of Rome’ with the enclitic -ሂ. ንዌጥን is the 1cp imperfect (or jussive; the two look alike here) of ወጠነ ‘begin’; the next verb ንንግርክሙ ‘we tell you’ is ነገረ + -ክሙ ‘you pl.’ in the 1cp jussive/subjunctive (ንንግር; the imperfect would be ንነግር) (?) follows without a conjunction, ‘we begin (to) tell you’. ዘሰማዕነ ‘that which we heard’, ወዘረከብነ ጽሑፈ ‘and that which we found written’ (ጽሑፍ ‘written’), ዘርኢነ ‘that which we saw’. The narrator names three sources: report, document, eyewitness.

sentences.t: መንግሥተ ፡ ሮምሰ ፡ ለያፌት ፡ ወልደ ፡ ኖሕ ፡ ኮነት ፡ ክፍሉ ፡ ወመንግሥቱ ፤
sentences.l: kingdom-of Rome-but to-Japheth son-of Noah was(f) his-portion and-his-kingdom;
sentences.i: The kingdom of Rome, for its part, belonged to Japheth, the son of Noah, as his portion and his kingdom;
sentences.n: መንግሥተ is the construct of መንግሥት ‘kingdom’; -ሰ marks contrast (‘as for the kingdom of Rome’). ለያፌት ‘to Japheth’ (ለ- of possession) with ወልደ ኖሕ ‘son-of Noah’ in the construct. ኮነት is the feminine perfect of ኮነ ‘be’, agreeing with ‘kingdom’; ክፍሉ ‘his portion’ and መንግሥቱ ‘his kingdom’ are the predicate. The background is the division of the earth among Noah's sons (Genesis 10): the text does not itself spell out which lands fell to which son. The book comes back to this when it says the kingship will pass to ‘the tribe of Shem’ (unit 9).

sentences.t: ወእንዘ ፡ ይነብሩ ፡ ገብሩ ፡ አህጉረ ፡ ዐበይተ ፡ ዓሥሩ ፡ ወክልኤ ፡ ወእለ ፡ የዐብያ ፡ አህጒረ ፡ መንግሥቶሙ ፡ ዳርዮስ ፡ ሐነጸ ፡ አንጦክያ ፡ ወዲርስያ ፡ ወባርቶንያ ፡ ወሮምያ ፡ ወይነብሩ ፡ ህየ ፡ እለ ፡ ነግሡ ።
sentences.l: And-while they-dwell they-made cities great ten and-two; and-those-which they(f)-are-great(?) cities-of their-kingdom Darius built Antioch and-Dirsia and-Bartonia and-Romia; and-dwell there those-who reigned.
sentences.i: While they dwelt they built twelve great cities; and those that are greater than the other cities of their kingdom (?): Darius built Antioch, Dirsia, Bartonia and Rome; and those who reigned would dwell there.
sentences.n: ወእንዘ ይነብሩ ‘and while they dwell’; ገብሩ ‘they made’ (perfect 3mp of ገብረ); ዓሥሩ ወክልኤ ‘ten and two’, twelve (ዓሥሩ I take as the feminine ዐሥሩ, ክልኤ as the feminine ‘two’, agreeing with the feminine plural ‘cities’ (?)); Geʿez puts the smaller number last. The clause ወእለ የዐብያ አህጒረ መንግሥቶሙ is hard: እለ ‘those who’ + የዐብያ, which I read as a verb from ዐበየ ‘be great’; the ending -ያ is the 3fp imperfect (-ā, the cities treated as feminine plural, as in ይነሥኦን ‘them (f.)’, unit 44), so ‘those (cities) which are great’, with አህጒረ መንግሥቶሙ ‘the cities of their kingdom’ in the accusative of comparison or respect: ‘which surpass the (other) cities of their kingdom’ (?). A causative ‘enlarge’ would need አዐበየ. Also አህጉረ above against አህጒረ here, the same word spelled two ways. Names in Bezold's spelling: ዳርዮስ Darius; አንጦክያ Antioch; ዲርስያ and ባርቶንያ I cannot identify (?); ሮምያ is Rome. ይነብሩ ህየ እለ ነግሡ ‘those who reigned dwell there’, an imperfect that I take as continuing or habitual (‘would dwell’).

sentences.t: ወቊስጥንጥንያ ፡ እምድኅረ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ሐነጸ ፡ ቈስጠንጢኖስ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ በስሙ ፡ ሶበ ፡ አስተርአዮ ፡ ትእምርተ ፡ መስቀል ፡ በውስተ ፡ ፀብእ ፡ በአምሳለ ፡ ከዋክብት ፡ ጽሑፋን ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሰማይ ፡ ወድኅነሂ ፡ እምእደ ፡ ፀሩ ፤
sentences.l: And-Constantinople after Christ built Constantine king in-his-name when he-showed-him sign-of cross in-midst-of battle in-likeness-of stars written in sky and-he-was-saved-too from-hand-of his-enemy;
sentences.i: And Constantinople was built after Christ by King Constantine, in his own name, when the sign of the cross was shown to him in battle, in the likeness of stars written in the sky, and he was also delivered from the hand of his enemy;
sentences.n: The city is ቊስጥንጥንያ and the emperor ቈስጠንጢኖስ, two spellings in one sentence, in Bezold's text. ሐነጸ ‘built’ (perfect 3ms) takes the king as subject; በስሙ ‘in his name’. አስተርአዮ is the ʾastä- stem of ርእየ ‘see’ (‘appear, show oneself’) + ‘him’; the house entry reads ‘it appeared to him’, and with the accusative ትእምርተ it is either ‘he showed him a sign’ or ‘it appeared to him, a sign’ (?); the subject is not named (God or Christ understood (?)), and ትእምርተ መስቀል ‘sign-of cross’ is the thing shown. በውስተ ፀብእ ‘in the midst of battle’. ጽሑፋን is a plural ‘written, inscribed’, agreeing with ከዋክብት ‘stars’. The vision recalls the familiar tradition of Constantine and the cross before a battle; the text itself says only ‘in battle’ and does not name the place (?). The i puts the verb in the passive (‘was shown to him’) because the subject is not stated; the Geʿez verb is active. ወድኅነሂ ‘and he was also saved’ (ድኅነ ‘be saved’); -ሂ ‘too’.

sentences.t: ወእምአሜሃ ፡ ረሰዩ ፡ ማኅደሮሙ ፡ ህየ ፡ ነገሥተ ፡ ሮም ።
sentences.l: and-from-then they-made their-dwelling there kings-of Rome.
sentences.i: and from then on the kings of Rome made their dwelling there.
sentences.n: ወእምአሜሃ ‘and from then’ (እም- ‘from’ + አሜሃ ‘then’). ረሰዩ ‘they made, set’ (perfect 3mp of ረሰየ) with ማኅደሮሙ ‘their dwelling’ (ማኅደር + ‘their’) as object; ነገሥተ ሮም ‘kings-of Rome’ is the subject placed last.

sentences.t: ወውእቱ ፡ ዳርዮስ ፡ ኮነ ፡ ዘርኡ ፡ ብዙኀ ፡ ወእምዳርዮስ ፡ እስከ ፡ መዋዕለ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ኮኑ ፡ ፲ወ፰ ፡ ትውልድ ።
sentences.l: And-that Darius was his-seed many, and-from-Darius until days-of Solomon were 10-and-8 generation.
sentences.i: This Darius had a numerous seed, and from Darius to the days of Solomon there were eighteen generations.
sentences.n: ወውእቱ ዳርዮስ ‘and that Darius’; ኮነ ዘርኡ ብዙኀ ‘his seed was many’ (ብዙኅ ‘many’, here in the accusative). መዋዕለ ‘days-of’ is the construct of መዋዕል. The numeral ፲ወ፰ is 18, written with a ወ ‘and’ between the digits, spoken ዐሠርቱ ወሰመንቱ (ʿäśärtu wä-sämäntu); the noun ትውልድ ‘generation’ stays singular, as Geʿez does after a number, though the verb ኮኑ is plural. Darius is placed some eighteen generations before Solomon; the text does not say which Darius.

sentences.t: እምዘርአ ፡ ዚአሁ ፡ ተወልደ ፡ ብእሲ ፡ ዘስሙ ፡ ዘንበሬስ ፡ ወገብረ ፡ በጥበብ ፡ መጽሐፈ ፡ አስጠሎባ ፡ ወረሰየ ፡ ከዋክብተ ፡ ወመዳልወ ፡ ፀሐይ ፤
sentences.l: from-seed-of his was-born man whose-name Zänbäres and-made in-wisdom book-of astrolabe(?) and-set stars and-instruments-of sun;
sentences.i: From his seed a man was born whose name was Zenberes, and with wisdom he made a book of the astrolabe, and he set out the stars and the instruments of the sun;
sentences.n: እምዘርአ ዚአሁ ‘from the seed of him’ (ዚአሁ is the independent ‘his’). ተወልደ ‘was born’ (passive). ዘስሙ ‘whose name’ (ዘ- + ስሙ). ዘንበሬስ is Bezold's spelling; I cannot identify the man (?). መጽሐፈ is the construct of መጽሐፍ ‘book’; አስጠሎባ looks like Greek astrolabos, ‘astrolabe’ (?). ረሰየ ‘set, arrange’ takes ከዋክብተ ‘stars’; መዳልወ is the construct of መዳልው ‘balance, measure’, here read as ‘instruments for measuring the sun’ (?). The picture is an astronomer-sage whose learning leads to the next unit.

sentences.t: ወርእየ ፡ ዘደኃሪ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢትነብር ፡ መንግሥት ፡ ኀቤሆሙ ፡ ለደቂቀ ፡ ያፌት ፡ አላ ፡ ትፈልስ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ነገደ ፡ ሴም ።
sentences.l: and-he-saw what-is-latter that not-will-remain kingdom with-them, to-sons-of Japheth, but will-migrate to seed-of David, tribe-of Shem.
sentences.i: And he foresaw that the kingdom would not remain with them, with the sons of Japheth, but would pass to the seed of David, of the tribe of Shem.
sentences.n: ወርእየ ‘and he saw’; ዘደኃሪ ‘what is later, the future’ (ዘ- + ደኃሪ ‘last’). The ከመ-clause: ኢትነብር ‘will not remain’ (3fs imperfect, subject መንግሥት ‘kingdom’), ትፈልስ ‘will migrate, move’ (ፈለሰ), with ኀቤሆሙ ‘with them’ and ለደቂቀ ያፌት ‘to the sons-of Japheth’ in apposition. ዘርአ ዳዊት ‘seed-of David’ and ነገደ ሴም ‘tribe-of Shem’ are two constructs. Sem here is Shem the son of Noah, ancestor of Israel (cf. the sons of Noah in unit 3). This is the text's reason why Rome should be joined to David's house.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ርእየ ፡ ከመዝ ፡ ለአከ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ንሣእአ ፡ ወለትየ ፡ ለወልድከ ፤
sentences.l: And-when he-saw thus he-sent to David king and-said: take-(her?) my-daughter for-your-son;
sentences.i: And when he saw this, he sent to King David and said: Take my daughter for your son;
sentences.n: ወሶበ ‘and when’. ለአከ ‘he sent’ (perfect 3ms of ለአከ); ኀበ ‘to’. ንሣእአ is the imperative ንሣእ ‘take!’ with an extra አ that I cannot account for; this letter has it on many words (ሰላምአ, ሀበኒአ, ወልድከአ, ዘኣነግሥአ, ሮምያአ, ወይእዜኒአ), so it looks like a mark of the text, perhaps a long vowel or an editor's sign; I ignore it in the gloss. ወለትየ ‘my daughter’ (ወለት + -የ ‘my’); ለወልድከ ‘for your son’ (ለ- + ወልድ + -ከ). ‘David’ is named as the recipient although Solomon is the son meant; the story assumes Solomon's father still lives.

sentences.t: ወነሥኣ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወወሀቦ ፡ ለሰሎሞን ፡ ወልዲ ፤
sentences.l: and-took-her David king and-gave-(him) to-Solomon his-son;
sentences.i: and King David took her and gave her to Solomon, his son;
sentences.n: ወነሥኣ ‘and he took her’ (-ኣ = ‘her’). ወወሀቦ is ወሀበ + -ኦ ‘him’, a suffix that anticipates the following ለሰሎሞን (‘gave (her), to him, to Solomon’), the same pleonastic pattern as ሤሞ ለአድራሚ (unit 29), ሐተቶ ለቀዳማዊ (unit 47) and እፌንዎ ለአርዳሚስ (unit 21); the object ‘her’ is understood from ወነሥኣ. It is not a slip. ወልዲ is ‘son’ with a final -ዲ in place of -ዱ ‘his’ or -ድየ ‘my’; the same spelling recurs of Adrami (units 29, 37), so I read ‘his son’ and take it as a Bezold spelling (-ዲ for -ዱ; compare ፈቀዲ ‘they wished’ in unit 29). The glossary entry in an earlier part reads ወልዲ as ‘my son’ (-ዲ for -ድየ) (?); here, in third-person narration, ‘his’ is the sense that fits. The house of David is thus joined to the house of Japheth by marriage before Adrami's birth.

sentences.t: ወወለደ ፡ እምኔሃ ፡ ወሰመዮ ፡ አድራሚ ።
sentences.l: And-he-begot from-her and-named-him Adrami.
sentences.i: And he had a son by her and named him Adrami.
sentences.n: ወለደ ‘he begot’ with እምኔሃ ‘from her’; ወሰመዮ ‘and named him’ (ሰመየ + -ዮ). The name is አድራሚ here; unit 21 gives አርዳሚስ for the same son, and the two forms stand side by side in Bezold's text. I keep Bezold's spelling in l and use ‘Adrami’ in i; for the other spelling I give ‘Ardamis’. The son is Solomon's son by the daughter of the Roman sage (the text does not call her a princess), a counterpart to Menelik, Solomon's son by the Queen of Sheba.

sentences.t: ወሞተ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ቀዳሚ ፡ ወነግሠ ፡ ባልጠሶር ፡ ዘእምአዝማዲሁ ፡ ወኀጥአ ፡ ተባዕተ ፡ ውሉደ ፡ ዘይነግሥ ፡ ድኅሬሁ ፡ ዲበ ፡ መንበሩ ፤
sentences.l: And-died he first and-reigned Baltasor, of-his-kinsmen, and-lacked male children who-will-reign after-him on his-throne;
sentences.i: The former one died, and Baltasar, one of his kinsmen, reigned; and he had no male children who would reign after him on his throne;
sentences.n: ወሞተ ውእቱ ቀዳሚ ‘and that first one died’ (the earlier one, I take the king before Baltasar (?); ቀዳሚ ‘first, former’). ወነግሠ ‘and reigned’; the name is ባልጠሶር here; later it is በልጠሶር and በልጣሶር, Bezold's three spellings of Belshazzar / Baltasar. ዘእምአዝማዲሁ ‘who (is) of his kinsmen’ (ዘ- + እም- + አዝማድ ‘kinsmen’ + ‘his’). ኀጥአ ‘he lacked’ (ኀጥአ usually ‘err, sin, miss’; ‘lack’ is my reading from context (?)). ተባዕተ ውሉደ ‘male children’; ዘይነግሥ ‘who would reign’ (ዘ- + imperfect); ዲበ መንበሩ ‘on his throne’.

sentences.t: ወይቀንእ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይንግሡ ፡ ድኅሬሁ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ አቡሁ ።
sentences.l: and-he-was-jealous that not-they-reign after-him sons-of his-father.
sentences.i: and he was jealous that the sons of his father should not reign after him.
sentences.n: ይቀንእ ‘he is jealous’ (the imperfect, used in narrative), with ከመ ኢይንግሡ ‘that they not reign’ (jussive of ነግሠ). ደቂቀ አቡሁ ‘sons-of his-father’ is, literally, his father's sons, which can mean his brothers or his father's other descendants; the text does not say which, and I leave the phrase literal. The sense is that Baltasar wants to bar a rival line from the throne, hence the foreign bridegroom he now asks for.

sentences.t: ወለአከ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ጽሒፎ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ ሰላምአ ፡ ለዕበየ ፡ መንግሥትከ ፡ ወለጥበብከ ፡ ክብርት ፤
sentences.l: And-he-sent to Solomon king, writing, saying: peace to-greatness-of your-kingdom and-to-your-wisdom honored;
sentences.i: He sent to King Solomon, writing and saying: Peace to the greatness of your kingdom and to your honored wisdom;
sentences.n: ጽሒፎ is the gerund (‘having written, writing’) of ጸሐፈ, with no object expressed; እንዘ ይብል ‘saying’. ሰላም ‘peace’ is the greeting formula, with the same extra አ (ሰላምአ). ለዕበየ መንግሥትከ ‘to the greatness-of your kingdom’ (ዕበይ ‘greatness’ in the construct) and ለጥበብከ ክብርት ‘to your honored wisdom’; ክብርት ‘honored, precious’. This is the style of a letter between kings, and the same one Solomon uses in unit 33.

sentences.t: ወይእዜኒአ ፡ ሀበኒአ ፡ ወልድከአ ፡ ዘኣነግሥአ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ሮምያአ ፤
sentences.l: and-now give-me your-son whom-I-make-king over city-of Rome;
sentences.i: and now give me your son, whom I shall make king over the city of Rome;
sentences.n: ወይእዜኒ ‘and now’ (ይእዜ + -ኒ). ሀበኒ ‘give me’ (imperative of ወሀበ + -ኒ). ወልድከ ‘your son’. ዘኣነግሥ is ዘ- ‘whom’ + the 1cs imperfect of አንገሠ ‘make king’ (the causative of ነግሠ). The extra አ again on four words. ሀገረ ሮምያ ‘city-of Rome’ is the construct (the same Rome as ሮም, here ሮምያ).

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ አንሰ ፡ ስእንኩአ ፡ ወሊደ ፡ ተባዕት ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ፫ ፡ አዋልድ ፡ ወእሁቦ ፡ እምአዋልድየ ፡ ዘፈቀደ ፡ ወእሁቦ ፡ መንበርየ ፡ ወይከውን ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ወዘርኡ ፡ እምድኅሬሁ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ሮምያ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፡ ወሶበ ፡ አንበባ ፡ ለይእቲ ፡ ክርታስ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ኀለየ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ ለእመ ፡ ከላእክዎ ፡ ወልድየ ፡ ይልእክ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ሠረቅ ፡ ወይሁቦ ፡ ወልዶ ፡ ወትበጥል ፡ እንተ ፡ መከርኩ ፤
sentences.l: for I-but I-am-unable to-beget male except 3 daughters and-I-give from-my-daughters whom he-wished and-I-give throne-my and-he-will-be king he and-his-seed after-him in city-of Rome until forever; and-when he-read that letter king Solomon he-thought saying: if I-withhold-him my-son he-will-send to king-of east and-he-give-him his-son and-will-be-void what I-counselled;
sentences.i: for I, for my part, am unable to beget a male child, except for three daughters; I shall give him whichever of my daughters he wishes, and I shall give him my throne, and he and his seed after him will be king in the city of Rome for ever. When King Solomon read this letter he considered, saying: If I withhold my son, he will send to the king of the east, who will give him his own son, and what I have decided will be void;
sentences.n: This unit holds the end of the letter and Solomon's thought; the source has no ። at the join, between እስከ ለዓለም and ወሶበ, so I keep it one unit (about 44 words). ስእንኩ is 1cs of ሰአነ ‘be unable’ with ወሊደ ‘to beget’; ዘእንበለ ፫ አዋልድ ‘except three daughters’ (the numeral ፫ is 3; before the feminine plural አዋልድ the spoken form is probably ሠለስ, śäläs (?), as the glossary entry for ፫ has it for feminine nouns). ወእሁቦ ‘and I give him’ (1cs imperfect). አንበባ is አንበበ ‘read’ + -ā ‘it (f.)’, for the feminine ክርታስ ‘letter, papyrus’ (ለ- marks the object). ኀለየ ‘he thought’. ከላእክዎ is ከልአ ‘withhold’ + ‘him’, most likely the king of Rome, from whom the son is kept (ወልድየ ‘my son’ is then the second object), or else -ዎ anticipates ወልድየ (?); ንጉሠ ሠረቅ ‘king-of east’ (ሠረቀ ‘rise’, so ‘sunrise’); who is meant, and who gives whose son to whom, I read as: the eastern king will give his own son to Baltasar (?). ትበጥል ‘will be void’ (በጥለ ‘be void’ (?)); እንተ መከርኩ ‘that which I counselled / decided’.

sentences.t: ወይእዜሰ ፡ እሁቦ ።
sentences.l: And-now-but I-give-him.
sentences.i: But now I will give him.
sentences.n: ወይእዜሰ ‘and now, however’ (-ሰ contrastive). እሁቦ ‘I give him’ (1cs imperfect). Solomon's decision, after he hesitated, is given in one short clause, so I make it a unit.

sentences.t: ወመከረ ፡ ምስለ ፡ መማክርቲሁ ፡ ዘቤተ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወይቤሎሙ ፡ እስመ ፡ ወሀብነ ፡ ወልደነ ፡ ወደቂቀነ ፡ ለብሔረ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወኮነ ፡ በህየ ፡ መንግሥት ፡ ለእስራኤል ፤
sentences.l: And-he-took-counsel with his-counsellors, of-house-of Israel, and-said-to-them: since we-gave our-son and-our-sons to-land-of Ethiopia and-became there kingdom for-Israel;
sentences.i: He took counsel with his counsellors of the house of Israel and said to them: Since we gave our son and our sons to the land of Ethiopia, and a kingdom for Israel arose there,
sentences.n: መከረ ‘took counsel’; መማክርቲሁ ‘his counsellors’ (plural of መምከር + -ሁ); ዘቤተ እስራኤል ‘of the house-of Israel’ (ቤተ construct). እስመ ‘since, because’. ወሀብነ ‘we gave’; ወልደነ ‘our son’ is Menelik, I take (the earlier chapters of the book), ወደቂቀነ ‘and our sons’ the sons of the elders who went with him to Ethiopia (?). ብሔረ ኢትዮጵያ ‘land-of Ethiopia’. ወኮነ በህየ መንግሥት ‘and there came to be there a kingdom’; the text counts Ethiopia as Israel's second kingdom.

sentences.t: ወይእዜኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይኩን ፡ ለነ ፡ ሣልስ ፡ መንግሥት ፤
sentences.l: and-now that there-be for-us third kingdom;
sentences.i: and now, that there may be for us a third kingdom,
sentences.n: ወይእዜኒ ‘and now’; ከመ ይኩን ‘that there be’ (jussive of ኮነ); ለነ ‘for us’; ሣልስ is the ordinal ‘third’. The sentence is completed in the next unit (a third kingdom ‘for the city of Rome’); Israel's first kingdom is Jerusalem, the second Ethiopia.

sentences.t: ለሀገረ ፡ ሮሜ ፡ ወአነሂ ፡ እፌንዎ ፡ ለአርዳሚስ ፡ ወልድየ ፡ ዘይንእስ ፤
sentences.l: for-city-of Rome, and-I-too I-send-him to-Ardamis my-son who-is-young;
sentences.i: over the city of Rome; and I, too, will send Ardamis, my younger son;
sentences.n: ለሀገረ ሮሜ ‘for the city-of Rome’ (spelled ሮሜ, not ሮምያ). አነሂ ‘I too’ (አነ + -ሂ). እፌንዎ ‘I send him’ (1cs imperfect of ፈነወ + ‘him’); ለአርዳሚስ marks the object with ለ-. The name now appears as አርዳሚስ, not አድራሚ (see unit 12). ወልድየ ዘይንእስ ‘my son who is young’ (ዘ- + ንእሰ ‘be small, young’), taken as the younger of two sons: Solomon's elder son is Menelik, so ‘younger’ is natural here.

sentences.t: ወአንትሙኒ ፡ ኢታስተአክዩኒ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘቀዲሙ ፡ ዘነሣእክዎሙ ፡ ለደቂቅክሙ ፡ እስመ ፡ ይከውን ፡ ብፅዐ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘአእመሩ ፡ ስሞ ፡ ሰብአ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወኮንዎ ፡ ሕዝቦ ፤
sentences.l: And-you-too do-not-reproach(?)-me on-account-of what formerly which I-took-them your-sons, for will-be vow(?) for-God on-account-of that they-knew his-name people-of Ethiopia and-became-(his) his-people;
sentences.i: And you also, do not reproach me for what I did before in taking your sons; for it will be a vow to God, on account of the fact that the people of Ethiopia came to know his name and became his people;
sentences.n: ወአንትሙኒ ‘and you too’ (አንትሙ + -ኒ). ኢታስተአክዩኒ ‘do not (2mp) ... me’; the verb is አስተአከየ, which I take as ‘reproach, blame’ (?), from the context. በእንተ ዘቀዲሙ ዘነሣእክዎሙ ለደቂቅክሙ ‘on account of what formerly (it was) that I took them, your sons’; the ለ- marks the object. ብፅዐ I read as ‘vow, promise’ (?) (ብፅዓት); ‘blessing’ is the other possible sense. ዘአእመሩ ስሞ ‘that they knew his name’ (አእመረ ‘know’); ወኮንዎ ሕዝቦ ‘and became his people’ (ኮነ + ‘to him’, with ሕዝቦ ‘his people’). The argument is that sending the sons out, as to Ethiopia, spreads the knowledge of God; compare the phrase ‘people of God’ below.

sentences.t: ወከማሁ ፡ ሰብአ ፡ ሮምኒ ፡ ለእመ ፡ ወሀብኖሙ ፡ ደቂቅነ ፡ ይከውኑ ፡ ሕዝበ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወለነኒ ፡ ይትወሀብ ፡ ለነ ፡ ስም ፡ በተብህሎ ፡ ወበተሰምዮ ፡ ሕዝበ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: and-likewise people-of Rome-also if we-give-them our-sons they-will-be people-of God, and-to-us-also will-be-given to-us name by-being-called and-by-being-named people-of God;
sentences.i: and in the same way the people of Rome too, if we give them our sons, will become the people of God; and for us also a name will be given, in that we are called and named the people of God;
sentences.n: ወከማሁ ‘and likewise’; ሰብአ ሮምኒ ‘men-of Rome too’. ለእመ ‘if’; ወሀብኖሙ ‘we give them’ (perfect with ‘if’); ይከውኑ ‘they will be’; ሕዝበ እግዚኣብሔር ‘people-of God’ (construct). ወለነኒ ‘and for us also’; ይትወሀብ ‘will be given’ (passive imperfect). በተብህሎ ወበተሰምዮ ‘in being called and in being named’, two infinitives of the passive (tä-) stems with በ-. People of God echoes the biblical name of Israel (Hosea 2:23; 1 Peter 2:10) without citing it.

sentences.t: ነሥኡ ፡ መንግሥተ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወመንግሥተ ፡ ሮምያ ፡ ሕዝበ ፡ እስራኤል ፤
sentences.l: they-took kingdom-of Ethiopia and-kingdom-of Rome people-of Israel;
sentences.i: Let the people of Israel take the kingdom of Ethiopia and the kingdom of Rome;
sentences.n: I am uncertain of the form. ነሥኡ is the perfect 3mp (‘they took’); the imperative would be ንሥኡ, so the form itself does not support ‘take!’. ሕዝበ እስራኤል ‘people-of Israel’ can be the (construct) subject: ‘the people of Israel took ...’, a perfect of certainty or purpose after the conditions of unit 23, or a slip for the imperative (?). ወሀቡ in the next unit is either an imperative or a perfect (?). መንግሥተ ኢትዮጵያ ‘kingdom-of Ethiopia’ and መንግሥተ ሮምያ ‘kingdom-of Rome’ are constructs. A second possibility is that ሕዝበ እስራኤል is a vocative, ‘O people of Israel’ (the accusative-like construct), with ነሥኡ an imperative in perfect vowelling: that would fit the 2mp ወሀቡ and ደቂቅክሙ ‘your sons’ that follow, and the whole speech being addressed to the elders (?). I give the sense of the sentence (Israel's reach over both realms) with a hortatory ‘let’.

sentences.t: ወሀቡ ፡ ከመ ፡ ቀዳሚ ፡ ደቂቅክሙ ፡ መንእሳነ ፤
sentences.l: and-give as formerly your-sons young-ones;
sentences.i: and give, as before, your younger sons;
sentences.n: ወሀቡ is the imperative ‘give!’ (2mp of ወሀበ, ሀቡ with ወ-), though it could be the perfect ‘they gave’ (?). ከመ ቀዳሚ ‘as before, as formerly’; ደቂቅክሙ ‘your sons’; መንእሳነ ‘young ones’ (a plural of ንኡስ ‘small, young’, or of መንእስ ‘youth’ (?)). The young sons go, the middle-aged stay (next unit), and the elders had already gone to Ethiopia.

sentences.t: ወማእከላውያንሰ ፡ ይቁሙ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገርነ ፡ ወተንሥኡ ፡ ወመከሩ ፡ ወገብኡ ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፡ ንንግሮ ፡ ለእግዚእነ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ነገረ ፡ ወይግበር ፡ ፈቃዶ ።
sentences.l: and-the-middle-ones-but let-them-stand in city-our; and-they-arose and-counselled and-returned and-said-to-him: let-us-tell-him to-our-lord king this word and-let-him-do his-will.
sentences.i: But let those of middle age remain in our city. And they rose, took counsel and returned, and said to him: Let us tell our lord the king this matter, and let him do his will.
sentences.n: ማእከላውያን is ‘those in the middle’ (the middle generation), with -ሰ ‘but’; ይቁሙ ‘let them stand / stay’ (jussive of ቆመ); ውስተ ሀገርነ ‘in our city’. Then narration: ተንሥኡ ‘they arose’, መከሩ ‘took counsel’, ገብኡ ‘returned’ (perfects 3mp), ወይቤልዎ ‘and they said to him’. The speakers' words (ንንግሮ ‘let us tell him’, ዘንተ ነገረ ‘this word, this matter’, ወይግበር ፈቃዶ ‘and let him do his will’) are an offer to put the plan to the king; the addressee of ‘to him’ is not clear to me (?). ፈቃዶ ‘his will’ (ፈቃድ + ‘his’).

sentences.t: ወይቤሎሙ ፡ አስምዑኒ ፡ ዘትብሉ ።
sentences.l: And-he-said-to-them: let-me-hear what you-say.
sentences.i: And he said to them: Let me hear what you say.
sentences.n: ወይቤሎሙ ‘and he said to them’; አስምዑኒ is the causative imperative of ሰምዐ ‘hear’ with ‘me’: ‘let me hear’; ዘትብሉ ‘what you (pl.) say’. The king (Solomon) asks for their opinion.

sentences.t: ወይቤልዎ ፡ ነሣእከ ፡ መላህቅተ ፡ ቤትነ ፡ ወይእዜኒ ፡ ንሣእ ፡ እምእለ ፡ ይቴሐቱ ፡ ደቂቆሙ ፡ መንእሳነ ፤
sentences.l: and-they-said-to-him: you-took elders-of our-house, and-now take from-those who-are-lowly their-sons young;
sentences.i: And they said to him: You took the elders of our house; now take the young sons of those who are lowlier;
sentences.n: ነሣእከ ‘you took’; መላህቅተ is the construct of a plural ‘elders’ (from ልህቀ ‘grow great’), the reading of which I take from the context (?); ቤትነ ‘our house’. ንሣእ is the imperative ‘take’; እምእለ ይቴሐቱ ‘from those who are low’ (a tä-stem verb ‘be low, humble’, in the imperfect; the lemma ተሐተ is my guess without Dillmann (?)); ደቂቆሙ መንእሳነ ‘their sons, the young ones’. The speakers ask that the king take sons from lower-ranking families, not from the great houses.

sentences.t: ወሠምረ ፡ በዝንቱ ፡ ምክር ፡ ወገብረ ፡ ሎሙ ፡ በከመ ፡ ፈቀዲ ፡ ወሤሞ ፡ ለአድራሚ ፡ ወልዲ ፡ ወነሥአ ፡ እምእለ ፡ ይቴሐቱ ፡ መኳንንተ ፡ ቤተ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወረከቦ ፡ ዕፅ ፡ በስመ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ወወሀብዎ ፡ ካህነ ፡ እምነገደ ፡ ሌዋዊያን ፡ ዘስሙ ፡ አኪሚሔል ፡ ወአጽዐንዎ ፡ ዲበ ፡ በቅለ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፡ ባሕ ፡ ሕያው ፡ አበ ፡ ነጋሢ ፤
sentences.l: and-he-was-pleased with-this counsel and-did for-them as they-wished(?), and-appointed-him Adrami his-son and-took from-those who-are-lowly nobles-of house-of Israel; and-found-him wood in-name-of his-father Solomon; and-gave-him priest from-tribe-of Levites whose-name Akimihel; and-mounted-him upon mule-of king and-said-to-him: bah(?) living father-of king;
sentences.i: He was pleased with this counsel and did for them as they wished, and he appointed Adrami his son, and took nobles of the house of Israel from among the lowlier ones; and the wood (?) found him in the name of his father Solomon; and they gave him a priest from the tribe of the Levites, whose name was Akimihel, and mounted him on the king's mule, and said to him: Bah! May the father of the king live (?);
sentences.n: A long unit (36 words), unbroken in the source. ወሠምረ ‘he was pleased’; በከመ ፈቀዲ ‘as ... wished’, with ፈቀዲ perhaps ፈቀዱ ‘they wished’ (?). ሤሞ is ሤመ ‘appoint’ + ‘him’; ለአድራሚ marks the object. ወረከቦ ዕፅ በስመ አቡሁ ሰሎሞን is unclear: ረከበ ‘find, receive’ + ‘him’ with ዕፅ ‘wood’; as in ch. 70 I keep ‘wood’ and ‘found him in the name of his father’ and do not turn it into a sceptre (?). ዘስሙ አኪሚሔል ‘whose name Akimihel’ (Bezold; I cannot identify the priest). አጽዐንዎ ‘they mounted him’ (the causative of ጸዐነ / ጽዕነ ‘load, ride’: ‘made him ride’ (?)); በቅለ ንጉሥ ‘mule-of king’, and the mounting of the new king on the royal mule follows 1 Kings 1:33. ባሕ is unclear to me (?). ሕያው አበ ነጋሢ ‘living, father-of king’ (ነጋሢ is the singular ‘king’) is a cry of acclamation, read as a wish ‘may the king’s father (Solomon) live’ as in ch. 70; the exact sense is uncertain (?).

sentences.t: ወይቤሉ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ሕዝብ ፡ ርቱዕ ፡ ይደልዎ ።
sentences.l: And-they-said all people: right it-befits-him.
sentences.i: And all the people said: It is right; he is worthy of it.
sentences.n: ወይቤሉ ‘and they said’ (ሉ is the 3mp), ኵሉ ሕዝብ ‘all the people’. ርቱዕ ‘right, fitting’ is a predicate adjective. ይደልዎ ‘it befits him / he is worthy’ (ደለወ ‘be fitting’ + ‘him’). The people's assent seals the choice, as in an enthronement.

sentences.t: ወቀብእዎ ፡ ቅብአ ፡ መንግሥት ፡ ዕፍረተ ፡ ወአዘዝዎ ፡ ይዕቀብ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ሕገ ፡ መንግሥት ፡ ወአምሐልዎ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢያምልክ ፡ ባዕደ ፡ አማልክተ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ አምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ፤
sentences.l: And-they-anointed-him anointing-of kingdom, with-perfume, and-they-commanded-him let-him-keep all law-of kingdom, and-they-made-him-swear that not-he-worship other gods except god-of Israel;
sentences.i: They anointed him with the anointing of kingship, with perfume, and they charged him to keep all the law of the kingdom, and made him swear not to worship other gods except the God of Israel;
sentences.n: ቀብእዎ ‘they anointed him’ (ቀብአ); ቅብአ መንግሥት ‘anointing-of kingdom’ (construct) is the cognate object; ዕፍረተ ‘with perfume, ointment’ is in apposition. አዘዝዎ ‘they commanded him’; ይዕቀብ ‘let him keep’ (ዐቀበ); ሕገ መንግሥት ‘law-of kingdom’. አምሐልዎ ‘they made him swear’ (the causative of መሐለ ‘swear’); ከመ ኢያምልክ ‘that he not worship’; ባዕደ አማልክተ ‘other gods’ (ባዕድ is also ‘strange, foreign’; compare Exodus 20:3); ዘእንበለ ‘except’; አምላከ እስራኤል ‘god-of Israel’.

sentences.t: ወባረክዎ ፡ በከመ ፡ ባረክዎ ፡ ለዳዊት ፡ እኁሁ ፡ ወትእዛዘኒ ፡ በከመ ፡ አዘዝዎ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ አዘዝዎ ፡ ለአድራሚ ፡ ወአስተፋነውዎ ፡ እስከ ፡ ሐይቀ ፡ ባሕር ፨
sentences.l: and-they-blessed-him as they-blessed David, his-brother, and-commands-too as they-commanded-him likewise they-commanded Adrami, and-they-escorted-him until shore-of sea;
sentences.i: They blessed him as they blessed David his brother, and as for the commandments, as they commanded him, so they commanded Adrami; and they sent him off as far as the shore of the sea;
sentences.n: ወባረክዎ ‘they blessed him’; ለዳዊት እኁሁ ‘David, his brother’ (ለ- marks the object, እኁሁ ‘his brother’). Here I take ‘David’ to be Menelik, who in the book is crowned with the name David; the text does not say, so the identification is a reading (?). ወትእዛዘኒ ‘and the commands too’; በከመ ... ከማሁ ‘as ... likewise’. አስተፋነውዎ ‘they sent him off’ (the astä- stem of ፈነወ ‘send’; ‘escort’ is the sense I give it (?)); ሐይቀ ባሕር ‘shore-of sea’ (ሐይቅ ‘shore’). The single ፨ ends the unit mid-text, as it does again below.

sentences.t: ወጸሐፈ ፡ ወለአከ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ሰላምአ ፡ ለበልጠሶር ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ሮሜ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-wrote and-sent saying king Solomon: peace to-Baltasor king-of Rome;
sentences.i: King Solomon wrote and sent, saying: Peace to Baltasar, king of Rome;
sentences.n: The order is ‘and he wrote and sent, saying, king Solomon’: the subject comes after the verb. ሰላምአ ‘peace’ with the extra አ again. ለበልጠሶር ‘to Baltasor’ (Bezold's second spelling, after ባልጠሶር in unit 13); ንጉሠ ሮሜ ‘king-of Rome’. This is the covering letter that goes with Adrami.

sentences.t: ንሣእአ ፡ ወልድየ ፡ አድራሚ ፡ ወሀቦ ፡ ወለተከ ፡ ወአንግሦ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ሮምያ ፤
sentences.l: take my-son Adrami and-give-him your-daughter and-make-him-king in city-of Rome;
sentences.i: Take my son Adrami, give him your daughter, and make him king in the city of Rome;
sentences.n: ንሣእአ ‘take!’ with the extra አ, not explained (see unit 10). ወሀቦ ‘give him’ (imperative ሀቦ with ወ-). ወለተከ ‘your daughter’ (ወለት + -ከ). አንግሦ ‘make him king’ (imperative of አንገሠ + ‘him’), with ውስተ ሀገረ ሮምያ ‘in the city-of Rome’. These are the terms of the proposal Baltasar made in unit 16.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ አፍቀርከ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ እምዘርአ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ አቡየ ፡ ወአነሂ ፡ ገበርኩ ፡ ፈቃደከ ፡ ወለአኩ ፡ ለከ ፡ ፲ወ፬ ፡ መኳንንቲሁ ፡ በየማኑ ፡ ወበፀጋሙ ፡ እለ ፡ የዐቅቡ ፡ ሕገ ፡ ምስሌሁ ፡ ወይትኤዘዙ ፡ ለከ ፡ በከመ ፡ ፈቀድከ ፨
sentences.l: for you-loved king from-seed-of David my-father, and-I-too did your-wish, and-I-sent to-you 14 his-nobles at-his-right and-at-his-left, who will-keep law with-him and-be-obedient to-you as you-wished;
sentences.i: since you loved a king from the seed of my father David; and I, too, have done what you wished, and I have sent to you fourteen nobles of his, at his right hand and at his left, who will keep the law with him and be obedient to you as you wished;
sentences.n: እስመ አፍቀርከ ‘for you loved’ (ፈቀረ a-stem አፍቀረ). ንጉሠ እምዘርአ ዳዊት አቡየ ‘a king from the seed-of David my-father’. ገበርኩ ፈቃደከ ‘I did your will’. ለአኩ ‘I sent’. ፲ወ፬ is 14, spoken ዐሠርቱ ወአርባዕቱ (ʿäśärtu wä-ʾärbaʿtu). በየማኑ ወበፀጋሙ ‘at his right and at his left’ (የማን, ፀጋም). የዐቅቡ ሕገ ‘who keep the law’; ይትኤዘዙ ‘be obedient’ (tä-stem of አዘዘ, ተኤዘዘ). The nobles are both the escort and the guarantors of the Law in Rome. The ፨ closes the unit.

sentences.t: ወበጽሑ ፡ ህየ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ልኡካነ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ሮሜ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ብዙኅ ፡ ክብር ፡ ወኵሉ ፡ ንዋይ ፡ ዘይትፈቀድ ፡ ለብሔረ ፡ ሮሜ ።
sentences.l: And-they-arrived there with envoys-of king-of Rome with much honor and-all goods which is-needed for-land-of Rome.
sentences.i: And they arrived there with the envoys of the king of Rome, with great honor and with all the goods needed for the land of Rome.
sentences.n: ወበጽሑ ‘and they arrived’ (በጽሐ ‘reach’); ህየ ‘there’ (the shore); ምስለ ‘with’; ልኡካነ ንጉሠ ሮሜ ‘envoys-of king-of Rome’. ብዙኅ ክብር ‘much honor’; ኵሉ ንዋይ ‘all goods’; ዘይትፈቀድ ‘which is desired, needed’ (passive ተፈቀደ); ለብሔረ ሮሜ ‘for the land-of Rome’. The Roman envoys, who had perhaps come to fetch him, meet Adrami's party at the coast (?); the text says only ‘they arrived there with the envoys’.

sentences.t: ወበጽሑ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ሮሜ ፡ ኀበ ፡ በልጣሶር ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወነገርዎ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ዘለአኮሙ ፡ ወአወፈይዎ ፡ ለወልዲ ፨
sentences.l: And-they-arrived city-of Rome to Baltasor king and-told-him all what he-sent-them and-presented-him to-his-son;
sentences.i: They reached the city of Rome, to King Baltasar, and told him everything for which Solomon had sent them, and presented his son to him;
sentences.n: ወበጽሑ ‘they arrived’ (accusative with ሀገረ ሮሜ). ኀበ በልጣሶር ንጉሥ ‘to Baltasor, the king’. ነገርዎ ‘they told him’; ኵሎ ዘለአኮሙ ‘all that he sent them’ (ዘ- ‘that which’). አወፈይዎ is አወፈየ ‘present, bring forward’ (?) + ‘him’, with ለወልዲ ‘his son’ (Solomon's, Adrami) in apposition to the suffix -ዎ, ‘they presented him, his son’; hence ‘presented his son to him’. The -ዲ spelling again as in unit 11. Bezold's spelling here is በልጣሶር.

sentences.t: ወተፈሥሐ ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ በልጣሶር ፡ ወወሀቦ ፡ ወለቶ ፡ እንተ ፡ ትልህቅ ፡ እንተ ፡ ስማ ፡ አድሎንያ ፡ ወገብረ ፡ ዐቢየ ፡ ከብካበ ፡ በከመ ፡ ዕበየ ፡ መንግሥቱ ፡ ወሤሞ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ሮምያ ፤
sentences.l: And-rejoiced exceedingly Baltasor and-gave-him his-daughter who elder who her-name Adlonia and-made great wedding-feast according-to greatness-of his-kingdom and-appointed-him over all city-of Rome;
sentences.i: Baltasar rejoiced exceedingly and gave him his daughter, the eldest, whose name was Adlonia, and held a great wedding feast befitting the greatness of his kingdom, and he set him over the whole city of Rome;
sentences.n: ወተፈሥሐ ፈድፋደ ‘and he rejoiced exceedingly’. ወሀቦ ወለቶ ‘gave him his daughter’; ወለቶ is ወለት + ‘his’ (-ቶ). እንተ ትልህቅ ‘who grows great, who is the elder’ (ልህቀ); ‘eldest’ in i is an inference from there being three daughters (?); እንተ ስማ ‘whose name’ (feminine ዘ-, ስማ ‘her name’); አድሎንያ is Bezold's spelling, the princess otherwise unknown (?). ከብካብ ‘wedding feast’; ዕበየ መንግሥቱ ‘the greatness of his kingdom’ (verb-noun ዕበየ). ሤሞ ‘appointed him’. In Bezold, ሀገረ ሮምያ is singular, ‘city’.

sentences.t: ወባረኮ ፡ ላዕሌሁ ፡ ወተፈሥሐ ፡ ቦቱ ፡ እስመ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ላሕዩ ፡ ወመንክር ፡ ጥበቢሁ ፡ ወጽኑዕ ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ በኀይሉ ፨
sentences.l: and-he-blessed-him over-him and-rejoiced in-him for good his-appearance and-wonderful his-wisdom and-strong exceedingly in-his-might.
sentences.i: He blessed him and rejoiced in him, for his appearance was fair and his wisdom wonderful, and he was exceedingly strong in his might.
sentences.n: ባረኮ ላዕሌሁ ‘he blessed him upon him’, i.e. pronounced a blessing over him. ተፈሥሐ ቦቱ ‘he rejoiced in him’. ሠናይ ላሕዩ ‘good (is) his appearance’ (ላሕይ ‘aspect, beauty’); መንክር ጥበቢሁ ‘wonderful (is) his wisdom’ (ጥበቢሁ is irregular: ጥበብ + -ሁ would be ጥበቡ; a plural or a variant of ጥበብ + ‘his’ (?)); ጽኑዕ ‘strong’ with ፈድፋደ ‘exceedingly’ and በኀይሉ ‘in his might’. The stock praise of a good king: beauty, wisdom, strength.

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ አሐተ ፡ ዕለተ ፡ ፈቀደ ፡ ያመክሮ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ፍትሕ ፡ ሶበ ፡ መጽአ ፡ ኀቤሁ ፡ ባዕለ ፡ ዐጸደ ፡ ወይን ፡ ወከልሐ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ እግዚእየ ፡ ተዐደወኒ ፡ ቃልከ ፡ ወአኅለቀ ፡ ዐጸደ ፡ ወይንየ ፡ አርሳኒ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ዮዳድ ፡ በአባግዒሁ ፤
sentences.l: And-then one day he-wished he-test-him in judgment when came to-him owner-of vineyard and-cried to-him saying: my-lord has-been-transgressed-against-me your-word and-destroyed vineyard-my Arsani son-of Yodad with-his-sheep;
sentences.i: Then one day he wished to test him in judgment, when the owner of a vineyard came to him and cried out to him, saying: My lord, your word has been transgressed against me, and Arsani son of Yodad has destroyed my vineyard with his sheep;
sentences.n: ወእምዝ ‘and after this’; ፈቀደ ያመክሮ ‘he wished that he test him’ (the subject is Baltasar, the object Adrami); በውስተ ፍትሕ ‘in the midst of judgment’. ባዕለ ዐጸደ ወይን ‘owner-of vineyard’, literally ‘lord of the enclosure of wine’ (ዐጸድ ‘enclosure, garden’). ከልሐ ‘cried out’. ተዐደወኒ ቃልከ is obscure; ተዐደወ ‘transgress, be passed over’, so ‘your word (your decree) has been trespassed against me’ (?). አኅለቀ ‘destroyed’; አርሳኒ ወልደ ዮዳድ ‘Arsani, son-of Yodad’ (names as spelled by Bezold, unknown to me (?)). The story is now a set-piece of royal judgment.

sentences.t: ወነዋ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቤትየ ፡ አኀዝኩ ፡ አባግዒሁ ፤
sentences.l: and-behold in my-house I-seized his-sheep;
sentences.i: and see, I have seized his sheep in my house;
sentences.n: ነዋ ‘behold’; ውስተ ቤትየ ‘in my house’; አኀዝኩ ‘I seized’ (1cs perfect of አኀዘ ‘take, hold’); አባግዒሁ ‘his sheep’ (አባግዕ + ‘his’, the plural of በግዕ). The vineyard owner says he is holding the sheep in his house.

sentences.t: ምንተ ፡ ትፈትሕ ፡ ላዕሌየ ።
sentences.l: What do-you-judge against-me?
sentences.i: What do you judge against me?
sentences.n: ምንተ ‘what’ (accusative of ምንት); ትፈትሕ ‘you judge’ (ፈትሐ); ላዕሌየ ‘upon me, against me’. The question reads ‘what judgment do you pass against me?’, perhaps ‘what is my penalty for seizing them?’ (?).

sentences.t: ወመጽአ ፡ ባዕለ ፡ አባግዕኒ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወከልሐ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ አግብእ ፡ ሊተ ፡ አባግዕየ ፤
sentences.l: And-came owner-of sheep-too to king and-cried saying: return to-me my-sheep;
sentences.i: And the owner of the sheep also came to the king and cried out, saying: Give me back my sheep,
sentences.n: ባዕለ አባግዕኒ ‘owner-of sheep too’ (the owner of the sheep, with -ኒ). ከልሐ is ‘cried out’ again. አግብእ ሊተ ‘bring back to me’ (a-stem imperative of ገብአ ‘return’); አባግዕየ ‘my sheep’.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ይነሥኦን ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘቦአ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዐጸደ ፡ ወይኑ ።
sentences.l: for he-takes-them on-account-of what it-entered into vineyard-his.
sentences.i: for he is holding them because they entered his vineyard.
sentences.n: ይነሥኦን ‘he takes them (f.)’ (the imperfect, -ን ‘them’, feminine plural); በእንተ ዘቦአ ‘on account of that (it) entered’, with a singular verb ቦአ for the plural sheep (a collective ‘flock’). ዐጸደ ወይኑ ‘his vineyard’ (ወይኑ is ወይን ‘vine’ + -ኡ ‘his’). So each side states the other's act.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎሙ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ሖሩ ፡ ተዋቀሱ ፡ በኀበ ፡ ንጉሥክሙ ፡ አድራሚ ፡ ወዘይቤለክሙ ፡ ግበሩ ።
sentences.l: And-said-to-them king: go argue at your-king Adrami and-what he-says-to-you do.
sentences.i: And the king said to them: Go and plead before your king Adrami, and do what he tells you.
sentences.n: ወይቤሎሙ ንጉሥ ‘the king said to them’ (Baltasar). ሖሩ ‘go’ (imperative 2mp); ተዋቀሱ ‘dispute, plead with each other’ (ተዋቀሰ), perhaps ‘go and have it out’ (?). በኀበ ንጉሥክሙ ‘before your king’; ዘይቤለክሙ ‘what he says to you’; ግበሩ ‘do (it)’. Baltasar gives the case to Adrami, as the means of the test announced in unit 40.

sentences.t: ወሖሩ ፡ ወተዋቀሱ ፡ በቅድሜሁ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-went and-disputed before-him;
sentences.i: They went and pleaded before him;
sentences.n: ሖሩ ‘they went’ (perfect 3mp); ወተዋቀሱ ‘and they disputed’; በቅድሜሁ ‘before him’ (ቅድሜ ‘front’ + ‘his’).

sentences.t: ሐተቶ ፡ ለቀዳማዊ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ እፎ ፡ በልዐ ፡ አባግዕ ፡ ዐጸደ ፡ ወይን ፤
sentences.l: he-questioned-him the-first saying: how ate sheep vineyard;
sentences.i: He questioned the first one, saying: How did the sheep eat the vineyard?
sentences.n: ሐተቶ ‘he questioned him’ (ሐተተ ‘examine, question’); ለቀዳማዊ ‘the first’ (the first plaintiff, ለ- marking the object, cf. ዘቀዲሙ). እፎ ‘how?’; በልዐ ‘ate’ (perfect 3ms with a plural subject, አባግዕ ‘sheep’); ዐጸደ ወይን ‘the vineyard’ (accusative, ‘enclosure-of wine’).

sentences.t: ቈጽለኑ ፡ ወሚመ ፡ አዕጹቀ ፡ ወሚመ ፡ ቆዐ ፡ ወሚመ ፡ ሥርወ ፡ እምጒንዲ ።
sentences.l: Leaves-?, or branches, or tendril, or root from-stock?
sentences.i: Was it the leaves, or the branches, or the tendril, or the root from the stock?
sentences.n: A list of the parts of the vine the sheep could eat. ቈጽለኑ is ቈጽል ‘leaf’ + -ኑ (question marker), ወሚመ ‘or’; አዕጹቀ ‘branches’; ቆዐ is a vine part whose meaning I do not know, here ‘tendril’, which is only a guess from the context (?); ሥርወ ‘root’; እምጒንዲ ‘from the stock, the trunk’ (እም- + ጒንድ). Bezold's spelling of ጉንዲ with ጒ. The details become the substance of the riddle in the next units.

sentences.t: አውሥአ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ባዕለ ፡ ዐጸደ ፡ ወይን ፡ በልዐ ፡ አዕጹቂሁ ፡ ምስለ ፡ አዕጹቀ ፡ ቆዑ ፡ ወኢያትረፈ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ አሕሩጊሁ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ጒንዲ ።
sentences.l: He-answered and-said-to-him owner-of vineyard: it-ate its-branches with branches-of its-tendril and-left-nothing except its-runners(?) with stock.
sentences.i: The owner of the vineyard answered him: It ate its branches with the branches of its tendril, and left nothing but its runners with the stock.
sentences.n: አውሥአ ‘he answered’ (a-stem of ወሥአ, as in the glossary); ወይቤሎ ‘said to him’. አዕጹቂሁ ‘its branches’ (አዕጹቅ + ‘his’); ምስለ አዕጹቀ ቆዑ ‘with the branches of its ቆዐ’. ኢያትረፈ ‘he did not leave over’ (a-stem of ተርፈ ‘remain’); ዘእንበለ ‘except’. አሕሩጊሁ I connect with ሐረግ ‘vine, creeper’, ‘its runners’ (?); ምስለ ጒንዲ ‘with the stock’. The vineyard owner's account is of a thorough devastation.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ሐተቶ ፡ ለባዕለ ፡ አባግዕ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ አማንኑ ፡ ከመዝ ።
sentences.l: And-again he-questioned-him the-owner-of sheep and-said-to-him: truly-? thus.
sentences.i: And again he questioned the owner of the sheep and said to him: Is it truly so?
sentences.n: ወካዕበ ‘and again’; ሐተቶ ‘he questioned him’; ለባዕለ አባግዕ ‘the owner-of sheep’ (ለ- as object). አማንኑ ከመዝ ‘truly, thus?’ (አማን ‘truly’ + -ኑ, the interrogative): ‘is it really so?’

sentences.t: ወአውሥኦ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ባዕለ ፡ አባግዕ ፡ እግዚእየ ፡ በልዐ ፡ አዕጹቀ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ቊጸሊሁ ።
sentences.l: And-he-answered-him and-said-to-him owner-of sheep: my-lord it-ate branches with its-leaves.
sentences.i: The owner of the sheep answered him and said: My lord, it ate branches with its leaves.
sentences.n: ወአውሥኦ ‘and he answered him’ (a-stem of ወሥአ with ‘him’). ወይቤሎ ባዕለ አባግዕ ‘and the owner-of sheep said to him’. በልዐ ‘it ate’ (the flock); አዕጹቀ ‘branches’; ምስለ ቊጸሊሁ ‘with its leaves’ (ቈጽል with ‘its’, spelled ቊጸሊ). So the sheep owner admits eating only the leaf and the branch, not the part the vineyard owner named.

sentences.t: ወአውሥአ ፡ አድራሚ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ወዝንቱሰ ፡ ይብል ፡ በልዓ ፡ ቆዐ ፤
sentences.l: And-answered Adrami and-said: and-this-one-but says it-ate tendril;
sentences.i: And Adrami answered and said: But this man says that it ate the tendril;
sentences.n: አውሥአ አድራሚ ‘Adrami answered’; ወዝንቱሰ ‘but this one’ (ዝንቱ + -ሰ). ይብል ‘he says’ (ይብል, the verb ‘say’); በልዓ ‘it ate’, which ends in -ā where the earlier units have በልዐ: I read it as the 3fp perfect (the flock as a feminine plural, as ይነሥኦን ‘them (f.)’, unit 44, treats the sheep), or as በልዐ + -ā ‘it (f.)’ anticipating ቆዐ (?); ቆዐ the same vine part as before (?). Adrami thus notes the conflict between the two accounts.

sentences.t: አማንኑ ፡ ከመዝ ።
sentences.l: Truly-? thus.
sentences.i: Is it so?
sentences.n: አማንኑ ከመዝ ‘truly? thus’, the same formula as in unit 50: Adrami repeats the question to the sheep owner. This clause ends at ።, so it is its own unit.

sentences.t: አውሥአ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ባዕለ ፡ አባግዕ ፡ አልቦ ፡ እግዚእየ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ይኩን ፡ ቆዐ ፡ ሠርጸ ፡ ጽጌ ፡ በልዐ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: Answered and-said owner-of sheep: no my-lord, except it-be tendril it-put-forth blossom it-ate.
sentences.i: The owner of the sheep answered and said: No, my lord; it ate it only when the tendril had put forth blossom (?).
sentences.n: አልቦ እግዚእየ ‘there is not, my lord’, i.e. ‘no, my lord’. ዘእንበለ ይኩን ቆዐ ሠርጸ ጽጌ በልዐ ‘except it be (that) the ቆዐ put forth blossom, it ate’; ሠርጸ ‘put forth, sprout’; ጽጌ ‘flower, blossom’. I read it as: the sheep ate the tendril only once it had flowered (?), which I leave as literal as the Geʿez allows, the construction being unusual (?). The part ends here, in the middle of the case, with the verdict still to come; the six ፨ marks close the chapter in Bezold and stay with this last unit.
